newsitem.title: UK: UK bank stocks jump after interest rate hike.
newsitem.headline: UK bank stocks jump after interest rate hike.

text.p: UK banking shares jumped on Tuesday, after the newly appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown lifted interest rates by 25 basis points and gave the central bank operational independence to set monetary policy.
At 1113 GMT, shares in Bank of Scotland jumped 13p to 389, having set a new peak at 391p earlier.

Abbey National Plc was up 19-1/2p to 857-1/2. Shares in Barclays Plc climbed 23-1/2p to 1168-1/2, while National Westminster Bank Plc advanced 21-1/2p to 749. Lloyds TSB Group, recovering an earlier deficit, added 15-1/2p to 571-1/2.

Elsewhere, shares in HSBC Holdings advanced 34p to 1717-1/2, after hitting a record 1722. Shares in Bank of Scotland rose 14p to 390, just one penny below the new peak set earlier. Standard Chartered Bank shares rallied 14-1/2p to 943, 2p below their record level set earlier.

Dealers and analysts said the rate hike and the Chancellor's move to give the central bank more independence gave investors confidence that the new Labour government is committed to fighting inflation.
"That means that it's easier for banks to keep their bad debts under control," said one bank analyst.
"And low inflation is also positive because low nominal growth in loan books means higher cash generating ability for banks," he added.
